project.title: All of Our Ancestors
project.subtitle: A deep-time atlas from LUCA to modern humans
project.aboutCaveat: These are representative lineage stages. Exemplar fossils are usually close relatives that illustrate what our actual ancestors may have resembled, not proven direct ancestors. The human lineage is bushy, not a clean ladder.

stages.name: LUCA
stages.fossils: No fossil; inferred from shared genes
stages.innovation: DNA/RNA/protein system, ribosomes, ATP metabolism, cellular life

stages.name: Proto-eukaryote
stages.innovation: Mitochondrial endosymbiosis begins; larger, more complex cells

stages.name: LECA
stages.fossils: No direct fossil; protosterol-biota as broad early-eukaryote signal
stages.innovation: Nucleus, mitochondria, cytoskeleton, membrane trafficking, likely sex

stages.name: Opisthokont ancestor
stages.fossils: No secure fossil; living analogues: fungi/animals/choanoflagellates
stages.innovation: Rear flagellum, phagocytosis, cell-signaling toolkit

stages.name: Choanoflagellate-like holozoan
stages.innovation: Collar cells, bacterial feeding, colony-forming potential

stages.name: Stem animal, sponge-grade
stages.innovation: Stable multicellularity, cell adhesion, developmental gene regulation

stages.name: Early eumetazoan-grade animal
stages.innovation: Tissues, nerves/muscles beginning, organized body axes

stages.name: Urbilaterian-like worm
stages.innovation: Bilateral symmetry, front/back body plan, directed crawling, likely through-gut

stages.name: Early deuterostome
stages.fossils: No perfect exemplar; Saccorhytus placement revised
stages.innovation: Deuterostome developmental pattern, pharyngeal-region innovations

stages.name: Early chordate
stages.innovation: Notochord, dorsal nerve cord, segmented muscles

stages.name: Early vertebrate/craniate
stages.innovation: Head, paired eyes, early backbone/skull tissues, active swimming

stages.name: Jawed vertebrate
stages.innovation: Jaws, teeth, paired appendage control, predatory feeding

stages.name: Bony fish ancestor
stages.innovation: Bony internal skeleton, tooth/jaw refinements, lung/swim-bladder lineage

stages.name: Lobe-finned fish
stages.innovation: Limb-like fin bones, stronger axial skeleton, air-breathing tendencies

stages.name: Fishapod
stages.innovation: Neck, flat skull, wrist-like fin bones, shallow-water ambush ecology

stages.name: Early tetrapod
stages.innovation: Digits, limbs, weight-bearing experiments, new ear/neck mechanics

stages.name: Reptiliomorph
stages.innovation: More terrestrial skeleton, stronger ribs/limbs, reduced water dependence

stages.name: Early amniote
stages.innovation: Amniotic egg, claws, drier skin, fully terrestrial reproduction

stages.name: Basal synapsid
stages.innovation: Single temporal opening; stronger jaw muscles — mammal-side skull begins

stages.name: Sphenacodontian
stages.innovation: Larger canines, deeper skull, dominant terrestrial predator body plan

stages.name: Early therapsid
stages.innovation: More upright limbs, differentiated teeth, enlarged temporal fenestra

stages.name: Theriodont
stages.innovation: More active metabolism, canine specialization, secondary-palate trend

stages.name: Basal cynodont
stages.innovation: Mammal-like teeth, secondary palate, larger jaw muscles, possible whisker/fur precursors

stages.name: Triassic cynodont survivor
stages.innovation: Burrowing, small active body, survival through P–T aftermath

stages.name: Advanced cynodont
stages.innovation: Better chewing, more upright gait, faster growth/metabolism

stages.name: Probainognathian
stages.innovation: Mammal-like tooth replacement, jaw-joint experimentation, smaller body

stages.name: Mammaliaform
stages.innovation: Dentary–squamosal jaw joint, middle-ear transition, hair, insectivory

stages.name: Early mammal-grade
stages.innovation: Larger braincase, sharper hearing, miniaturized nocturnal niche

stages.name: Therian stem
stages.innovation: Lineage toward placentals separates from marsupial line; arboreal/scansorial traits

stages.name: Early eutherian
stages.innovation: Placental-line anatomy, fur, climbing, tribosphenic molars

stages.name: Boreoeutherian ancestor
stages.fossils: No good body fossil; molecular node
stages.innovation: Placental diversification; primates + rodents/lagomorphs branch

stages.name: Primate stem
stages.innovation: Arboreal life, fruit/insect diet, grasping tendency after K–Pg

stages.name: True primate
stages.innovation: Nails, grasping hands/feet, forward-facing eyes, leaping/climbing

stages.name: Anthropoid
stages.innovation: Monkey/ape/human line: enhanced vision, shorter snout, enclosed eye sockets

stages.name: Catarrhine
stages.innovation: Old World monkey + ape line; two premolars; larger brain/body

stages.name: Early ape
stages.innovation: Tail loss, more mobile shoulders/back, ape-like climbing

stages.name: Great-ape stem
stages.innovation: Larger-bodied apes, suspensory climbing, great-ape face/dentition trends

stages.name: Hominin origin
stages.innovation: Smaller canines, possible early bipedality, human/chimp split zone

stages.name: Early hominin mosaic
stages.innovation: Bipedal traits plus grasping big toe; glorious weird middle

stages.name: Australopith biped
stages.innovation: Habitual bipedality, humanlike pelvis/knee, still small brain

stages.name: Early Homo
stages.fossils: LD 350-1 jaw, H. habilis, H. rudolfensis
stages.innovation: Bigger brain trend, smaller teeth, tools/stone-flaking ecology

stages.name: Long-legged human
stages.fossils: Turkana Boy, Dmanisi fossils, Java fossils
stages.innovation: Humanlike body plan, endurance walking/running, dispersal beyond Africa

stages.name: Middle Pleistocene Homo
stages.fossils: Sima de los Huesos, Kabwe, Bodo
stages.innovation: Large brains, big-game hunting, near sapiens–Neanderthal–Denisovan split

stages.name: Early Homo sapiens
stages.innovation: Modern face emerging, braincase becoming globular, complex tools

stages.name: Recent modern humans
stages.fossils: Skhul/Qafzeh, later African and Eurasian fossils
stages.innovation: Symbolic culture, language-rich societies, global dispersal, cumulative tech
